summary: AE + SE demo of Redwood Hosted API embeddings and reranker for ZephyrSearch, covered end-to-end flow, performance expectations, security, and next steps for a POC.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-01
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Head of Search - Zephyr), Tom Rivers (Principal Eng), Lina Gomez (Product), Jamal Ortiz (Eng Mgr)

Auto-summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + rerank flow, demoed sample dataset, discussed latency/cost and enterprise security needs; agreed to POC and data transfer steps.

Topics: embeddings model selection, item vs query embeddings, rerank model call patterns, caching, batching and expected unit-cost, SSO and audit logs, POC timeline.

[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you carving o-out the hour. I'm Alex Chen from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya, our search SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Maya Patel: Hey Alex, hey Priya, thanks. Good—busy week but excited to see how this might improve our relevance.
[00:00:18] Tom Rivers: Hi, quick note, we have about 40 mins, and then Lina has another call at 16:45, so maybe we keep Q&A to the end.
[00:00:26] Priya Raman: Perfect, we'll try to pace it. Quick agenda: we demo embeddings pipeline, show search + rerank flow, go over perf and cost, and leave 10 mins for security/questions.
[00:00:38] Jamal Ortiz: Sounds good.
[00:00:41] Alex Chen: Cool. First, can you—Maya or Tom—give us a quick snapshot of current infra and goals?
[00:00:48] Maya Patel: Sure. So ZephyrSearch runs a mixed infra: primary search index in Elastic Cloud, some vector store tests with Pinecone right now for semantic fallback. Our main problem is re-ranking for long-tail queries—relevancy drops and latency spikes during peak. We want to get consistent relevance, and keep p95 latency under 200ms for the user path. Cloud costs are also high.
[00:01:10] Tom Rivers: We have about 200M docs, embeddings per doc are around 1024 dims, batch updates nightly. Query traffic TTL is spiky—peak QPS ~2200.
[00:01:21] Priya Raman: Great, that helps. OK we'll jump into the demo—I'll share my screen.
[00:01:25] [00:01:30] Priya Raman: (screen share) Alright, this is Redwood Console. The demo uses our hosted embeddings endpoint and a reranker endpoint. The flow is: compute query embedding, do a k-NN recall from your vector store (we show integration options), then call our rerank API with top-k candidates and the original query.
[00:01:52] Priya Raman: I'm going to paste a sample request—note we support batched candidate lists and streaming responses for explanations.
[00:02:05] Maya Patel: Can you repeat the bit about streaming? We care about showing top result quickly and streaming the rest.
[00:02:12] Priya Raman: Yeah so streaming lets you return first token(s) of the reranker output as soon as they're available; for rerank we usually return scores and structured reason fields incrementally. It's not full token-by-token generative streaming like chat, but you can get progressive rank updates.
[00:02:33] [00:02:45] Priya Raman: Here's an example request payload. Note we include metadata per candidate (doc_id, source, snippet) and Redwood accepts either pre-computed embeddings or will compute embeddings inline if you prefer.
[00:02:58] Tom Rivers: If we send precomputed embeddings, can Redwood accept 1024-dim float32 and use quantized variants?
[00:03:06] Priya Raman: Yes, accepts float arrays; on our backend we support quantized runtime paths. For hosted we automatically pick quantization when it preserves quality per your workload. You can also pin model profiles.
[00:03:20] Jamal Ortiz: How about latency—if we send top 10 candidates and call the reranker, what p50/p95 numbers should we expect?
[00:03:28] Priya Raman: Good question. For a hosted rerank call with top-10 and 1024-dim, our typical p50 is ~20-35ms, p95 ~120-200ms depending on traffic and sequence length. We always recommend testing with your exact payload; we'll run a 1k-query benchmark to give you numbers.
[00:03:47] Maya Patel: That's promising; our p95 budget is 200ms so it's close. Cost-wise?
[00:03:53] Alex Chen: Cost is driven by token equivalent for reranker (model size) and embedding usage. We'll share an example pricing sheet—dedicated vs hosted differences. For hosted, you pay per embedding vector compute and per-rerank call. If you want predictable unit-costs we can discuss dedicated capacity.
[00:04:10] [00:04:20] Priya Raman: Now I'll demonstrate a live rerank. I'm sending a sample query "best noise-cancelling earbuds under $150" and passing top 8 recall candidates. You'll see score diffs and explanation.
[00:04:35] [00:04:45] (demo: console shows request/response)
[00:04:46] Priya Raman: Response back—here's top doc, score 0.87, next 0.61. We highlight snippet spans that matched intent, and a short rationale string.
[00:04:58] Tom Rivers: Is the rationale generated or deterministic? We need it to be reproducible for A/B tests.
[00:05:03] Priya Raman: The rationale is model-derived but we also offer deterministic feature-based signals in the payload if you prefer—feature scores are stable. Rationale text can vary but we log raw scores and features for evals.
[00:05:16] Maya Patel: What about retraining indexes—how do you manage embedding drift?
[00:05:21] Priya Raman: We recommend a periodic re-embed of updated docs and a hybrid approach: use feature-stable signals for core ranking and reranker to adjust ordering. Redwood Optimize will flag quality regressions and recommend re-embed cadence.
[00:05:34] [00:05:45] Priya Raman: I want to show the API example now. This is the hosted embeddings endpoint. One call returns a 1024-dim vector; we support 768/1024/1536 dims across models.
[00:05:59] Alex Chen: One note on integrations—you mentioned Elastic and Pinecone. Redwood integrates with both; we also have connectors to S3 and can push vectors into vector stores or serve via our API as a pure-ranked endpoint.
[00:06:12] Jamal Ortiz: For the POC, we'd prefer Redwood to host the reranker but keep vectors in Pinecone for recall. Is that a supported pattern?
[00:06:19] Priya Raman: Totally supported—recall with Pinecone, call Redwood rerank with candidate ids and snippets. We have example SDKs and a small middleware shim to format chunks.
[00:06:30] Maya Patel: Security—SAML/SSO for console, and we need SOC2 and audit logs. Also, data residency: some docs must stay in EU.
[00:06:40] Alex Chen: We support SSO (SAML/OAuth), RBAC at route level, audit logs, and KMS integrations for keys. For residency, our hosted regions include EU and US, and we can route by policy; Private deployments are available for stricter needs. We'll send the security whitepaper.
[00:06:57] [00:07:10] Tom Rivers: What's the data retention policy on embeddings and rerank payloads? We need to ensure transient storage only for 30 days, with options to disable logging for PII-sensitive queries.
[00:07:18] Priya Raman: You can configure request logging and retention per account; for POC we can disable logging and not persist payloads. For enterprise customers we provide audit logs and retention controls.
[00:07:33] Maya Patel: Sounds good. One thing—our search team wants to test rerank ordering consistency between A and B. How do rollouts work?
[00:07:41] Alex Chen: Redwood supports canary rollouts and A/B by traffic splits, plus automatic fallback if p50/p95 deviates beyond thresholds. You can pin model versions and fallback to a cheaper variant.
[00:07:53] [00:08:05] Priya Raman: Back to perf: We can enable caching of prefix KV states for repeated queries; also batching—if you have burst traffic we can autoscale or use dedicated reserved pools to keep latency tight.
[00:08:18] Jamal Ortiz: For dedicated, how long to provision?
[00:08:22] Alex Chen: Typically a few weeks for reserved capacity depending on region and GPU selection; hosted is immediate.
[00:08:30] [00:08:45] (demo: showing Optimize recommendations)
[00:08:46] Priya Raman: Here's Redwood Optimize—based on workload it suggests model and quantization that balance cost/quality, plus batching configs for your QPS shape. It also surfaces prompt sets where quality regressed.
[00:09:00] Maya Patel: That regression alerting is attractive. We have concern about hallucinations in rationale text—can we rely on feature-based signals instead?
[00:09:09] Priya Raman: Yes, you can disable text rationale and rely on numeric feature vectors. Optimize will surface which combination gives best nDCG on your eval set.
[00:09:24] [00:09:35] Tom Rivers: Okay, timeline—if we start a POC next week, what's realistic?
[00:09:40] Alex Chen: If you can provide the sample query set and a subset of documents, we can stand up a POC in ~3-7 business days: 1 day to provision, 2-3 days to run benchmarks and tweak configs.
[00:09:53] Maya Patel: We can get the anonymized query set ready by Friday.
[00:09:57] Jamal Ortiz: And we'll need the benchmark scripts.
[00:10:00] Priya Raman: We'll send the scripts and a quickstart repo after call.
[00:10:05] [00:10:15] (customer question volley)
[00:10:16] Lina Gomez: Pricing question—if we run 1M rerank calls/month and 10M embedding calls/month, ballpark?
[00:10:24] Alex Chen: I'll send a conservative estimate in the pricing doc; there's also volume tiers and a committed Dedicated option that significantly lowers per-call costs. We'll include modeled numbers for your traffic.
[00:10:36] Maya Patel: One last security nit—can we get a redacted SOC2 and pen test report?
[00:10:42] Alex Chen: Absolutely. We'll attach them to the email along with the SOW draft.
[00:10:50] [00:11:00] Priya Raman: Alright, going to show a couple edge cases—the reranker when candidate set includes near-duplicates, and how we pass metadata to avoid demoting fresh content. (demo)
[00:11:18] Priya Raman: You can attach document freshness and boost fields in the candidate payload; reranker will use them as signals.
[00:11:27] Tom Rivers: Are there throttles for large batched rerank calls? We may batch for backstage ML scoring jobs.
[00:11:33] Priya Raman: We have rate limits and concurrency controls; for large offline batches we recommend a batch ingestion path that is cheaper and avoids live SLOs.
[00:11:46] [00:11:55] (brief silences and minor transcription artifacts)
[00:12:10] Maya Patel: This was really informative—appreciate the specifics.
[00:12:15] Alex Chen: Great. Quick recap of next steps: we'll send pricing and SOW, security docs, benchmark scripts, and schedule the POC kickoff. Priya will own the benchmark and Tom will provide the dataset.
[00:12:29] Priya Raman: I'll also drop a sample Postman and node SDK snippet.
[00:12:33] Tom Rivers: Perfect.
[00:12:36] [00:12:40] Alex Chen: Anything else before we close?
[00:12:43] Lina Gomez: No, that covers it.
[00:12:45] Alex Chen: OK thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD with the attachments and proposed POC dates.
[00:12:52] Maya Patel: Thanks, bye.
[00:12:54] Tom Rivers: Bye.

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-heard words and timestamps roughly every 30-90s per Fireflies export style.
